blocks.content: Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and has grown into one of the largest railway networks in the world.

items: Frequently tested: Zone headquarters matching questions (e.g., South Eastern Railway - Kolkata, North Central Railway - Prayagraj).
Crucial for exams: Standard track gauge dimensions — Broad Gauge (1676 mm), Meter Gauge (1000 mm), Narrow Gauge (762 mm / 610 mm).
Important date: The first electric train operated in India on February 3, 1925 between Bombay CST and Kurla.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first passenger train in India ran between Mumbai (Bori Bunder) and Thane on April 16, 1853, covering a distance of 34 km.
Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and is organized into 19 administrative zones.
Broad Gauge (1.676 m) accounts for the majority of the total route kilometerage of Indian Railways.
Bholu, an elephant dressed as a railway guard holding a lamp, serves as the official mascot of Indian Railways.
